title: Signature Soundex encoding — Phonetic Search
description: Signature original — Soundex maps a name to a letter-plus-three-digits code by keeping the first letter and encoding consonant groups. Vowels and h/w are dropped, adjacent same-coded letters merge, and the result is padded or cut to four characters. 'Smith' and 'Smyth' both yield S530, which is why census-era record linkage still leans on it. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# Phonetic search: Soundex codes group names that sound alike.
def soundex(name):
    name = name.upper()
    if not name: return "0000"
    table = str.maketrans("AEIOUYHW", "00000000")
    table2 = str.maketrans("BFPVCGJKQSXZDTLMNR", "111122222222334556")
    first = name[0]
    coded = name.translate(table).translate(table2)
    digits = "".join(ch for ch in coded if ch != "0")
    merged = first
    for ch in digits:
        if ch != merged[-1]: merged += ch
    return (merged + "000")[:4]
names = ['Smith','Smyth','Smythe','Jones','Schmidt']
query = "Smith"
qc = soundex(query)
print("Soundex(%r) = %s" % (query, qc))
for n in names:
    mark = "  <-- sounds alike" if soundex(n) == qc else ""
    print(f"{n:12} -> {soundex(n)}{mark}")
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.

title: Signature Metaphone algorithm — Phonetic Search
description: Signature original — Metaphone encodes English pronunciation rules: silent letters drop, 'ph' becomes 'F', 'sh' and 'th' get their own codes. It handles the quirks Soundex ignores, so 'Thompson' and 'Tomson' align while 'Smith' and 'Smyth' still do. Metaphone is the default upgrade when Soundex precision disappoints. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
